questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted somewhere far away and with lots of nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I had an amazing time at Mac and meet a lot of great people
The trails were really nice and the fall colours was to die for

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't really have any problems and the few things I needed help with I got help pretty fast

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We got a tour and had a day where all exchange students met and got all the needed info
also a lot of mails with useful stuff

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found a place with airbnb which worked out really well!
If you're going for a single semester you probably wont get on-campus housing so find something off campus and do it early
can recommend Westdale or Dundas

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
If possible try not to get housing in downtown its a bit sketchy
watch out for scams on FB and Airbnb

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
They post the courses for registration and you just build your courses from what times match 
Some classes got posted a bit later than others which was really confusing

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could find out how to do the process on their website but you could also email them

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had no problems except one class where registration didn't open till later which i didn't know

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just plan your courses ahead of time and ask if any of them open up later

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Honestly thought the most of the courses were pretty easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching was pretty similar but they did grade for a bunch of different stuff like attendance and participation
Most of the exams were MC

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Astronomy: the big questions
Philosophy: Meaning in life
Computational thinking
Medicinal Anthropology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Astronomy: the big questions is really fun and a free course
Philosophy: Meaning in life has an amazing prof. and I honestly had a great time in that course

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really join any clubs but here was a whole lot of them but spend most of my time with the other exchange students (there was around 150)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A whole bunch of clubs and the uni hosts quite a lot of social events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some of the outdoor club trips they're really nice especially the canoe trip

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see Toronto and the nature cause its amazing

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Felt like it was pretty easy though some things were different from back home like there being sugar in all bread

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Just go up and talk to them they are so easy going and chatty 
If you're not that social try joining a club or some trips

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Some of the food items available were pretty different was the biggest challenges
And that their pilsner is pretty bad 
And their style in clothes is pretty bad

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved how outgoing people were and there was some pretty weird and fun stuff to do (go to medieval times that was so fun)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to make an exchange student groupchat, participate in the things people do together in the start even if it's a bit intense and go out to different restaurants there was some amazing ones (especially in Toronto (can recommend Raiku))

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just have fun

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Without a doubt all the amazing people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Had some problems with traveling though that was personal things though

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was a great experience would definitely recommend

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
